subject: physics

moments.title: Michelson-Morley find no ether
moments.body: Light supposedly travels through a luminiferous ether. They build a precision interferometer to detect Earth's motion through it. The expected fringe shift is 0.4; the observed shift is essentially zero.
moments.takeaway: Light has the same speed in every direction, no matter how you move.

moments.title: Einstein's relativity paper
moments.body: A 26-year-old Swiss patent clerk publishes 'On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies'. He assumes the speed of light is the same for all observers and derives time dilation and length contraction. He cites no one. Three months later he adds a four-page addendum: E = mc^2.
moments.takeaway: Space and time fuse into spacetime. Mass and energy fuse into one quantity.

moments.title: Minkowski's spacetime
moments.body: Einstein's old maths teacher (who once called him a 'lazy dog') gives relativity its geometric form. Spacetime is a four-dimensional manifold; the interval between events is invariant.

quote.text: Henceforth space by itself, and time by itself, are doomed to fade away into mere shadows.

moments.takeaway: Spacetime is one object. The geometry comes first; everything else follows.

moments.title: Hafele-Keating clocks
moments.body: Atomic clocks flown around the world on commercial airliners return with measurably different elapsed times from a reference clock, confirming relativistic time dilation. Cost: about $8,000, mostly for tickets.
moments.takeaway: Time dilation is real. Every GPS satellite must correct for it.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Special relativity is the framework for all of high-energy physics. Particle accelerators reach 0.99999...c. GPS applies 38 microseconds/day of relativistic correction.
now.open_questions: Is Lorentz invariance exact, or does it break near the Planck scale?

reflection: Einstein had no lab and few equations beyond high-school algebra in 1905. What enabled his breakthrough that hundreds of better-equipped physicists missed?
